title: Identify Patterns and Trends

header.html: Use the Analyze feature in Power BI; Use grouping, binning, and clustering; Use AI visuals; Use reference lines, error bars, and forecasting; Detect outliers and anomalies; Use Copilot to summarize the underlying semantic model
the official PL-300 study guide (skills measured as of April 20, 2026)

toc.title: AI visuals: which one answers which question
Reference lines, error bars and forecasting

html:
1AI visuals: which one answers which question

Power BI has four AI visuals, and each one answers a different kind of question. The exam tests the match.

Visual Question it answers Key settings
Key influencers What drives a metric to be high, low or a given category? Analyze, Explain by, Expand by; tabs Key influencers and Top segments
Decomposition tree How does one measure break down across dimensions, in any order? Analyze is the measure; Explain by holds the dimensions; AI splits choose High value or Low value
Smart narrative Can I read the story of a visual or page as text? Text with dynamic values that follow the filters
Q and A visual Can users ask a question in plain language? A question box and suggested questions
  • Key influencers supports categorical or continuous analysis and does not support DirectQuery.
  • In a decomposition tree you can lock a level, so the AI does not change it.
  • Smart narrative is the older mode. The narrative visual with Copilot (Module 10) is the newer one.
  • Q and A experiences are going away in February 2027. Microsoft recommends Copilot instead.
Exam tip

. Key influencers explains why a metric is high or low; the decomposition tree breaks one measure down and lets you drill into the biggest part. If the question says "drivers" or "what affects", choose key influencers.

Exam tip

. Q and A experiences are going away in February 2027, and Microsoft recommends Copilot. Expect Copilot as the modern answer for natural language questions.

2Analyze, grouping, binning and clustering

Analyze explains a change with one right-click. Right-click a data point on a bar or line chart, choose Analyze, then pick one option.

Option What it does
Explain the increase Finds the factors behind a rise at that point
Explain the decrease Finds the factors behind a fall at that point
Find where this distribution is different Finds what makes that distribution unlike the others

The default output is a waterfall chart. Analyze is not supported on DirectQuery, on a live connection or on a model with row-level security. The first data point has no insight.

Grouping, binning and clustering create categories for a visual.

Feature How you make it Result
Grouping Ctrl+select data points, then Group A field named "(groups)"; edit the groups; an Other group holds the rest
Binning Choose a numeric or time field, then set the Bin size A field named "(bins)"; not available for measures
Clustering Use a scatter chart Automatically groups similar points; you can choose the number of clusters
Exam tip

. Grouping is hand-picked, binning is equal-size ranges, clustering is automatic on a scatter chart. Bins work on numeric and time fields, never on measures.

3Reference lines, error bars and forecasting

All of these live in the Analytics pane of a selected visual. Which visual supports which item is a favorite question.

Item Where it works Notes
Constant line X or Y axis A fixed value you type, such as a target
Min, max, average, median, percentile lines Visuals with the pane Calculated from the data; percentile lines are for imported data
Trend line Line, area and column charts Shows the direction of the data
Forecast Line chart only Set the forecast length and the confidence interval
Symmetry shading Scatter chart only Shades the plot to show where one axis is higher than the other
Error bars Bar, column and line charts Show a range of uncertainty around each value
Anomalies Line chart only See section 4
Exam tip

. Forecast works only on a line chart. A trend line works on line, area and column charts; error bars on bar, column and line charts.

4Outliers, anomalies and Copilot summaries

Outliers are values far from the rest. Show them on a scatter chart, where outliers sit away from the main group. Add average, median or percentile lines to judge the distance.

Anomaly detection finds unusual points in a time series. Turn it on in the Analytics pane.

Requirement Detail
Visual A line chart with a time series axis
Data At least 4 data points
Settings A sensitivity setting; Explain by gives possible explanations
Does not work with A legend, multiple or secondary values, or a forecast or reference lines on the same chart

To summarize the semantic model, ask Copilot to summarize it. Copilot can also add descriptions to measures. The requirements are the same as in Module 10:

  • A paid Fabric capacity F2 or higher, or Premium P1 or higher. A trial, or Pro or PPU alone, is not enough.
  • The Copilot tenant setting turned on, and a supported region.
  • After you buy capacity, Copilot can take up to 24 hours to appear.
  • Row-level and object-level security still apply to what Copilot can see.
Exam tip

. Anomaly detection fails when the chart has a legend, a secondary value, a forecast or a reference line. Remove them first.

Exam tip

. Copilot needs a paid Fabric capacity F2 or higher, or Premium P1 or higher. Pro or PPU alone does not turn it on.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A retailer's line chart shows monthly sales, and March is much higher than February. An analyst wants to see which factors explain the rise. What should the analyst do?

  • AAdd a trend line in the Analytics pane and compare it with March
  • BTurn on a forecast in the Analytics pane and read the March value
  • CRight-click the March point and choose Analyze, then Explain the increase
  • DCreate a bin on the Month field and compare the bins for March
Show the answer

Answer: C. Analyze with Explain the increase finds the factors behind a rise at one data point; trend lines, forecasts and bins do not explain a change.

S2A finance team wants to learn which customer attributes are most associated with a low satisfaction rating. Which visual should it add?

  • AA decomposition tree with the rating as the only measure
  • BA Q and A visual with a suggested question about ratings
  • CA smart narrative on the page that shows ratings
  • DA key influencers visual with the rating in Analyze
Show the answer

Answer: D. Key influencers ranks the fields that drive a metric; a decomposition tree only breaks a measure down.

S3A finance team wants to extend monthly revenue three months ahead, with a confidence interval. Which visual type must it use?

  • AA line chart showing revenue by month
  • BA column chart showing revenue by month
  • CAn area chart showing revenue by month
  • DA scatter chart showing revenue by month
Show the answer

Answer: A. The forecast option is available on line charts only.

S4A line chart with a date axis shows daily orders for three regions in a legend. An analyst turns on anomaly detection and gets no results. What should the analyst do?

  • ASwitch the chart type to a scatter chart of orders
  • BRemove the legend so the chart has one series
  • CAdd a forecast to the same chart for the orders
  • DAdd a constant line at the average order count
Show the answer

Answer: B. Anomaly detection does not work with a legend, so one series on a time axis is needed; a forecast or a constant line would also block it.

S5An analyst has a numeric Age column and needs a column chart of customers by ten-year ranges. What should the analyst create?

  • AA cluster on the Age column in a scatter chart
  • BA group made by Ctrl+selecting some age values
  • CA bin on a measure that averages customer age
  • DA bin on the Age column with a bin size of ten
Show the answer

Answer: D. Binning cuts a numeric field into equal-size ranges, and it cannot be applied to a measure.

S6A team has Pro licenses and a trial capacity. A developer wants Copilot to summarize a semantic model and add measure descriptions, but Copilot is unavailable. What does the team need?

  • AA paid Fabric capacity F2 or higher
  • BA Pro license for each developer
  • CA Premium Per User license for each user
  • DA trial extension for the capacity
Show the answer

Answer: A. Copilot needs a paid Fabric capacity F2 or higher, or Premium P1 or higher; a trial, Pro or PPU alone is not enough.

5.2 Recall questions

R1Which pane holds the forecast, trend line and error bars?

Show the answer

The Analytics pane.

R2Which chart type is the only one that supports a forecast?

Show the answer

The line chart.

R3Name three situations where Analyze is not supported.

Show the answer

DirectQuery, a live connection and a model with row-level security.

R4What is happening to Q and A experiences in February 2027?

Show the answer

They are going away, and Microsoft recommends Copilot.

R5Which kind of field cannot be binned?

Show the answer

A measure.

R6On which chart type does clustering work?

Show the answer

A scatter chart.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Analyze right-click a point on a bar or line chart; Explain the increase, Explain the decrease, Find where this distribution is different; waterfall; not on DirectQuery, live connection or RLS
Key influencers Analyze, Explain by, Expand by; not DirectQuery; answers "what drives it"
Decomposition tree measure in Analyze, dimensions in Explain by; High value or Low value splits; lock levels
Smart narrative, Q and A text summary with dynamic values; Q and A experiences going away in February 2027, Copilot recommended
Grouping, binning, clustering group by Ctrl+select; bins for numeric and time fields, not measures; clusters on a scatter chart
Analytics pane forecast on line charts only; trend line on line, area and column; error bars on bar, column and line
Anomalies line chart with a time axis, at least 4 points; no legend, secondary values, forecast or reference lines
Copilot summary summarize the model, add measure descriptions; paid F2 or higher, or P1 or higher
